commit.author: Ed Baker <edwbaker@gmail.com>
commit.message:
Do not inherit the bit rate from a lossless input (#68)

av_audio_convert() could not write Ogg Vorbis at all: the encoder is
given the decoder's bit rate, and for a lossless input that is the raw
PCM rate (1411200 for 44.1 kHz 16-bit stereo). libvorbis has no setting
near that, so vorbis_encode_setup_managed() fails and the conversion
dies in avcodec_open2() with "encoder setup failed".

The encoder choice was not the problem; av already resolves ogg to
libvorbis. The same input converts fine as soon as the bit rate is
plausible, and a lossy source whose own bit rate is already sane was
never affected.

Only inherit the input bit rate when the input is not lossless, using
the codec descriptor's AV_CODEC_PROP_LOSSLESS. An explicit bit_rate is
honoured as before; otherwise the encoder picks its own default. This
also makes 48 kHz wav to .opus work.

The documented default, "will match input", could never hold for a
lossless input into a lossy encoder, so the parameter docs are updated.

Note that wav to mp3 without an explicit bit_rate changes: libmp3lame
was silently clamping 1411200 to its 320 kbps ceiling and now uses its
own 128 kbps default.
